concerns.concern: The paper's own activation energy for polar nanoregion relaxation (76 meV) implies these regions would be completely frozen at the temperatures where the Tc memory is written (≤10 K) and where illumination is done. That contradicts the claim that they realign with the gate field.
concerns.quote: The PNRs that "collectively align with the external field and reverse their orientations as V_g switches sign" would be completely frozen in the regime where the T_c memory is written

concerns.concern: Thermally activated oxygen-vacancy ionization with the reported 236 meV activation energy would also be frozen well below ~70 K. The dielectric-loss parameters therefore cannot describe the low-temperature dynamics, and the authors should report the attempt rates and confront these timescales.
concerns.quote: Thermally activated OV ionization with E_a2 = 236 meV is likewise frozen well below ~70 K.

concerns.concern: The fitted dark-relaxation time barely changes between 12 and 180 K and is comparable to the observation window. This suggests it is set by the fitting window rather than by physics. Longer windows or stretched/two-component fits are needed.
concerns.quote: This is a classic sign that the time constant is set by the fitting window, not the physics.

concerns.concern: The ΔR/R₁ peaks at 35 K and 95 K each rest on a single data point, and those traces look anomalous or noisier than their neighbours. Denser temperature sampling and repeat measurements are needed before claiming a coincidence with the dielectric peaks.
concerns.quote: The ΔR/R₁ "peaks" at 35 K and 95 K (Fig. 4b) are each defined by one data point.

concerns.concern: Across all protocols, Tc appears to track mobility or sheet resistance inversely. Tc may therefore simply be a function of disorder, which would make the PNR pairing model unnecessary. A plot of Tc versus μ and versus R_s for all states is requested.
concerns.quote: fully consistent with T_c being a single function of μ or disorder

concerns.concern: The text says the relaxation time has minima at 35 K and 95 K. The figure instead shows a maximum at 95 K, immediately after a minimum at ~90 K.
concerns.quote: In Fig. 4c, τ is actually maximal at 95 K (~1.38 × 10³ s), immediately after a minimum at ~90 K.

concerns.concern: The dielectric measurement probes the whole 0.5 mm substrate, while the 2DEG lies within nanometres of the surface. Nothing shows that either loss peak originates near the interface.
concerns.quote: Nothing shows that either loss peak originates near the interface.

concerns.concern: LED heating is visible, so the sample temperature during illumination must be reported and a purely thermal origin of the reset ruled out. Suggested tests are power and wavelength dependence and a comparison with an equivalent thermal excursion.
concerns.quote: a purely thermal origin of the reset should be excluded

concerns.concern: PNR alignment, remanent polarization and the internal gating field are only inferred, never measured. Direct probes such as SHG, piezoresponse or polarization–voltage loops are requested.
concerns.quote: PNR alignment, remanent polarization and an "internal gating field" are inferred, never measured.

concerns.concern: The model is internally inconsistent. Randomizing PNRs lowers Tc, implying alignment of either sign raises it, yet the two oppositely aligned remanent states have different Tc. The authors must state whether the polarization sign or the degree of alignment controls Tc.
concerns.quote: The authors should state which PNR quantity controls T_c: the net polarization sign or the degree of alignment.

concerns.concern: The ~76 meV loss peak matches known off-centre impurity-dipole relaxations in KTaO₃, such as Li⁺ reorientation. It may be a bulk extrinsic effect rather than interfacial PNRs.
concerns.quote: This would be a bulk extrinsic effect, not interfacial PNRs.

concerns.concern: The ~100 K loss peak could be a Maxwell–Wagner or contact relaxation artefact rather than oxygen-vacancy ionization. Controls such as a bare substrate, different thicknesses and Cole–Cole or equivalent-circuit analysis are suggested.
concerns.quote: could plausibly be a Maxwell–Wagner or contact relaxation

concerns.concern: The title's "erasure of superconductivity" overstates the result. Only a gate-trained Tc increment of about 70 mK (~7%) is erased.
concerns.quote: What is actually erased is a gate-trained T_c increment of ~70 mK (~7%).

concerns.concern: "Complete erasure" is not demonstrated. It requires showing that Tc after illumination returns to the pristine value, but only relative shifts are shown.
concerns.quote: This requires showing that T_c after illumination returns to the pristine value (1.017 K).

concerns.concern: LED output varies with temperature, so the temperature-dependent illumination data were taken at uncontrolled photon flux. This undermines comparison of ΔR/R₁ across temperatures.
concerns.quote: The temperature-dependent illumination data (Fig. 4, Supp. Fig. 5) were therefore taken at uncontrolled flux

concerns.concern: All data appear to come from a single sample. Additional samples, ideally with different oxygen-vacancy densities to test the model directly, are needed.
concerns.quote: All data appear to come from a single sample.

concerns.concern: Linearity of the loop size with ε is expected for almost any charge-trapping mechanism, because the induced charge scales with ε. It therefore does not single out oxygen vacancies.
concerns.quote: Linearity is therefore expected for almost any charge-trapping mechanism and does not single out OVs.

concerns.concern: The steeper loop-size dependence below 35 K can be explained trivially by ε saturating in the quantum-paraelectric regime while the loop size keeps growing.
concerns.quote: Any Δ_L(T) that keeps growing while ε plateaus will show an apparent upturn when plotted against ε.

concerns.concern: The integrated irreversible gate current should be compared with the geometric capacitive charge and the measured Δn·A. It may exceed the capacitive charge by an order of magnitude, so where the extra charge goes, including possible leakage, must be established.
concerns.quote: A ~10 nA transient lasting tens of seconds could exceed the capacitive charge by an order of magnitude.

concerns.concern: Hall carrier density is higher at −50 V than at +50 V, the opposite of capacitive doping, and the swing exceeds the expected magnitude. This is unexplained.
concerns.quote: This is the opposite of naive capacitive doping, and the ~4% swing exceeds the expected ~1%.

concerns.concern: KTO(111) 2DEGs are multiband, so single-field Hall n and μ are effective quantities, and percent-level changes may reflect subband redistribution. Field-dependent Hall data with two-band fits are needed.
concerns.quote: Field-dependent Hall data with two-band fits are needed before n and μ are interpreted separately.

concerns.concern: The dielectric analysis neglects the temperature-dependent series resistance of the 2DEG and contacts.
concerns.quote: The series resistance of the 2DEG and contacts, which changes with temperature, is neglected.

concerns.concern: Leakage current at the nA scale adds directly to the measured dielectric loss.
concerns.quote: Leakage current, which is nA-scale per Supp. Fig. 3, adds directly to the loss.

concerns.concern: The 5 V ac excitation is large for a quantum paraelectric with field-dependent ε. An excitation-amplitude dependence is requested.
concerns.quote: The 5 V ac excitation is large for a quantum paraelectric with field-dependent ε.

concerns.concern: The measured ε (~1600–2000) is well below typical low-temperature bulk KTO values, and this is unexplained.
concerns.quote: The authors should explain why (fringe fields, a dead layer, or geometry).

concerns.concern: After training, the two remanent states differ by only ~0.2–0.8% in R_s. The large Tc change is mostly a one-time conditioning effect, so the memory window is small.
concerns.quote: The large T_c change is largely a one-time conditioning effect.

concerns.concern: First-sweep forming and irreversible back-gating are well documented in SrTiO₃ interfaces and explained without PNRs. This literature should be discussed, and the novelty relative to ref. 30 clarified.
concerns.quote: The authors should discuss this literature and clarify what is new relative to ref. 30.

concerns.concern: The absence of persistent photoconductivity at 2 K conflicts with the claim that photons can activate the processes even at extremely low temperatures.
concerns.quote: The absence of persistent photoconductivity at 2 K conflicts with the statement that photons can activate these processes "even at extremely low temperatures."

concerns.concern: For device relevance, the authors should state whether erasure works below or near Tc, or only at 10 K.
concerns.quote: they should also state whether erasure works below or near T_c, or only at 10 K.

concerns.concern: The LED emission wavelength at cryogenic temperature should be measured rather than assumed to be 1.97 eV.
concerns.quote: The LED's emission wavelength at cryogenic temperature should be measured rather than assumed to be 1.97 eV.

concerns.concern: Endurance, retention at operating temperature, and the need to warm to 10 K for erasure should be stated before neuromorphic applications are claimed.
concerns.quote: Endurance (8 cycles shown), retention at the operating temperature, and the need to warm to 10 K for erasure should be stated

concerns.concern: The main text says gate cycles decrease n, while the Supplement says they increase n. The dependence on the initial state should be stated and discussed.
concerns.quote: Both may be correct, but the dependence on initial state should be stated and discussed.

concerns.concern: Plotting two monotonic functions of temperature against each other generically produces apparent correlations.
concerns.quote: Plotting two monotonic functions of T against each other generically produces apparent correlations.

concerns.concern: Gate sweep rates, hold times and the temperature at which each Tc memory step was written should be specified, since they matter for any kinetic interpretation.
concerns.quote: Specify gate sweep rates, hold times and the temperature at which each T_c memory step was written

concerns.concern: Uncertainties on the activation energies should be reported. The Peak 2 Arrhenius fit spans only a narrow 1/T range.
concerns.quote: Report ω₁ and ω₂ and the uncertainties on E_a. The Peak 2 Arrhenius fit spans a narrow 1/T range.

concerns.concern: The statement that loops persist up to ~100 K conflicts with the Supplement, which discusses loops up to 180 K.
concerns.quote: The ~100 K loop-persistence statement (Fig. 1g) should be reconciled with Supp. Fig. 2

concerns.concern: The van der Pauw/FEM correction factor and its uncertainty should be given.
concerns.quote: Give the van der Pauw/FEM correction factor and its uncertainty.

concerns.concern: Gate cycling protocols are inconsistent: the Supplement describes cycles going to +50 V first, while Fig. 1 starts toward −50 V.
concerns.quote: The protocols should be made consistent or clearly distinguished.

concerns.concern: The threshold voltage is given as −17 V in the main text but roughly −15 V in the Supplement.
concerns.quote: The threshold is −17 V in the main text and Fig. 2g but "roughly −15 V" in Supp. Note 3.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3d caption should say that the vertical dashed line marks ε at 35 K, not T = 35 K.
concerns.quote: the "vertical dashed line" marks ε(35 K), not T = 35 K; the caption should say so.

concerns.concern: A sheet-resistance label is wrong in Supp. Note 4 (R_s^b should be R_s^a).
concerns.quote: "higher sheet resistance R_s^b = 856 Ω" should be R_s^a.

concerns.concern: The LED is misnamed as a "laser emitting diode".
concerns.quote: "Red laser emitting diode (LED)" should be "light-emitting diode."

concerns.concern: Supplementary Figure 5 is labelled "Extended Figure 5" in its caption.
concerns.quote: "Supplementary Figure 5" is labelled "Extended Figure 5" in its caption.

concerns.concern: A sentence in the Discussion is duplicated.
concerns.quote: the sentence about dielectric loss "further reinforcing this picture" is duplicated.

concerns.concern: Units for sheet resistance are used inconsistently.
concerns.quote: Units are inconsistent (Ω vs Ω·sq⁻¹).

concerns.concern: The manuscript contains several typos.
concerns.quote: Typos: "would facilitates," "memrisitive," "illlumination," "Suppelementary," "that the it is."
